create_skyweave.journal.cargo.kelp.title: Kelp
create_skyweave.journal.cargo.kelp.descr:
Have at least 1 Kelp in your inventory at once.

Dried kelp is used to craft Mechanical Belts, which carry items between Create machines. Processing kelp therefore supports automation as well as its use as food.

Keep some living kelp if you want to grow a continuing supply in water. Turning the entire first harvest into dried kelp removes that immediate planting stock.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.cargo.funnel.des:
Have at least 1 Andesite funnel in your inventory at once.

An Andesite Funnel transfers items between an inventory and the space in front of it, such as a belt or depot. It provides a way to feed machines and collect their outputs without moving every item by hand.

Facing and placement determine where items enter or leave. Start with a short transfer between storage and one machine before extending the same arrangement into a longer line.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.cargo.filter.des:
Have at least 1 Filter in your inventory at once.

A Filter describes which items compatible Create logistics blocks should accept or reject. It can keep a processing ingredient separate from other material moving through the same system.

Use filters at points where mixed output needs to split into different destinations. The filter selects items; the attached machine or transport block performs the transfer.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.cargo.package.de:
Complete Create's Packager advancement.

A Packager forms packages from an attached inventory. This can group goods for handling without changing how those goods were produced.

Try a short loading and unpacking route before extending it to remote storage. Packaging your own goods is separate from Delivery Table contracts, which supply their own schematic cargo.

The machine credits its recorded player. An already completed advancement counts; the journal does not measure throughput or a complete production line.
create_skyweave.journal.cargo.dock.title: Docking connectors
create_skyweave.journal.cargo.dock.descr:
Have at least 2 Docking connectors in your inventory at once.

Docking Connectors work in pairs, aligning and locking together to make a rigid connection. The connected structures remain separate rather than merging into one contraption.

Once locked, the connection can transfer items and fluids in either direction with insertion and extraction arranged on the two sides. Retracting either connector releases the dock.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.cargo.deliveries:
Right-click delivery table.

Craft a Delivery Table to browse jobs for supplied schematic cargo. Offers use discovered village destinations; they do not buy the output of your farms or workshops.

Right-click the Delivery Table to inspect the available jobs. Check the supplied cargo, pickup point, destination and reward before accepting a shipment.

Transport the supplied cargo to its destination; missing cargo reduces the reward. Allow space and lifting capacity for the load, and keep enough fuel or another means of travel for the return journey.

Completion checks the block interaction, not a completed delivery.
create_skyweave.journal.electricity.roto:
Have at least 1 Generator induction rotor in your inventory at once.

The Generator Induction Rotor produces electricity when spun in a magnetic field. It belongs to an assembly with coils, a commutator and a generator clutch; a rotor on its own is not a working generator.

Mechanical Crafters make the rotor from andesite alloy, copper coils and a shaft. A functioning generator also needs excitation current in its stator coils to establish the magnetic field.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.electricity.wire:
Have at least 2 Wire connectors in your inventory at once.

Wire Connectors provide attachment points for Power Grid wires. They let you route a connection through intermediate supports instead of running one uninterrupted span.

A connector does not generate or store energy. The circuit still needs a source, a connected load and the appropriate wiring.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.electricity.moto:
Have at least 1 Electric motor in your inventory at once.

An Electric Motor converts Power Grid electricity into rotational power for machinery. Its speed depends on the supplied voltage.

A motor lets electrical wiring carry power to a machine that would otherwise need a continuous shaft connection. The generator and circuit still have to support the machine's load.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.electricity.batt:
Have at least 1 Battery in your inventory at once.

A Power Grid Battery stores electrical energy for later use. It can buffer a circuit when generation and demand occur at different times.

The battery's voltage changes as it discharges. Check the requirements of connected devices rather than treating a stored charge as a constant-voltage supply.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.electricity.use_:
Right-click circuit design table.

Open the Circuit Design Table to inspect its circuit-design workspace. Placing components in a design requires those components in your inventory.

The table can write the current design into a Circuit Schematic. That schematic describes a circuit to build; opening the table does not create or power it.

Completion checks the block interaction, not a completed circuit.
Have at least 1 Ion thruster in your inventory at once.

An Ion Thruster produces directional thrust from FE energy while enabled by redstone. It needs an electrical supply instead of a tank of liquid fuel.

Its recipe includes a Precision Mechanism and electrical components. Producing the thruster is only part of the build: the craft also needs a compatible energy connection and a way to control thrust.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.electricity.run_:
Complete Power Grid's Electric Motor advancement.

An Electric Motor converts electrical supply into rotation. Complete the circuit and supply enough power for the connected mechanical load.

Test the motor separately before relying on it for flight or a production line. A motor transfers energy; a battery only stores energy supplied from elsewhere.

The machine credits its recorded player. An already completed advancement counts; the journal does not measure throughput or a complete production line.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.portable:
Obtain a Portable Engine of any color.

A Portable Engine supplies rotation without a fixed waterwheel or windmill. It can drive propellers and mechanisms on a craft when supplied and connected correctly.

Reserve space for operating supplies and transmission. A compact power source does not remove the craft's need for lift, control or a return fuel budget.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.solid.de:
Have at least 1 Solid-fuel thruster in your inventory at once.

A Solid-fuel Thruster burns items supplied from the rear and uses redstone as an on/off control. Opening its rear hatch with a wrench allows it to draw fuel from a container behind it.

This provides propulsion without first setting up liquid-fuel processing. Fuel storage and access to the rear intake still need space in the craft.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.resin.de:
Have at least 4 Pine resin in your inventory at once.

Crushing a spruce log has a 60% chance to produce one Pine Resin. This route requires Crushing Wheels; a Millstone does not process logs into resin.

Spruce saplings make the wood supply renewable. The mason building in Sky Villages can contain a spruce sapling, providing another exploration route when nearby islands lack spruce trees; that building is not guaranteed in every village.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.turpenti:
Have at least 1 Turpentine bucket in your inventory at once.

Mix one Pine Resin with 250 mB of water in a Basin to make 250 mB of turpentine. The recipe needs a powered Mechanical Mixer but no heat; four successful batches fill one bucket.

Tanks and pipes store the fuel and supply Liquid Thrusters. Resin production still needs Crushing Wheels and spruce logs, so establish that supply before relying on turpentine for repeated journeys.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.liquid.d:
Have at least 1 Liquid thruster in your inventory at once.

The Liquid Thruster produces directional thrust when supplied with turpentine and enabled by redstone. Pipes can replenish its fuel supply from storage.

Turpentine production depends on pine resin, water and mixing in a Basin. A fuel tank can support a trip, but repeated travel also needs a way to make and load more fuel.

Groups of eight or 27 Liquid Thrusters can form larger thruster assemblies. These assemblies accept fluid through their rear intake, so reserve that side for fuel delivery.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.tank.des:
Have at least 1 Fluid tank in your inventory at once.

Fluid Tanks store liquids for processing and transport. Adjacent tanks can form a larger reservoir, with pipes providing a way to fill and drain it.

Storage separates the rate of fuel production from the rate at which a machine consumes it. A turpentine reserve can supply a thruster while the fuel-processing line is idle.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.stirling:
Have at least 1 Stirling engine in your inventory at once.

A Stirling Engine produces rotational power while heated from below. When that heat is removed, it stops generating rotation.

The engine converts an available heat source into power for shafts and machines. Its usefulness depends on maintaining that heat wherever the machinery is operating.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.steering:
Have at least 1 Steering wheel in your inventory at once.

A Steering Wheel provides controlled rotational output when you turn it. It is an input for mechanisms, rather than a device that automatically steers an entire aircraft.

Connect that output to the mechanism you want to adjust. Comparators can also read the wheel's angle, providing an input for redstone control.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.controll:
Obtain a Linked Controller and 2 Redstone Links. The conditions are recorded independently.

A Linked Controller sends inputs to matching Redstone Link frequencies. Connect the receiving signals to mechanisms such as thrusters or transmission controls.

Test each input while the craft is secured. A controller does not automatically provide steering, altitude hold or a safe response when an input is released.

With an empty hand, hold Shift and right-click a frequency slot to open its menu. Ghost slots and personal presets choose frequencies without consuming the selected items; relocation supports ordinary Redstone Links within one world or ship.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.sensor.d:
Obtain an Altitude Sensor, Velocity Sensor or Gimbal Sensor.

Sensors make a craft's height, movement or orientation available to control mechanisms. Choose the measurement that matches the adjustment you want to make.

Start by observing the output before connecting it to propulsion. A sensor is an input to a control system; owning one does not demonstrate an autopilot.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.verdigri:
Obtain 4 Verdigris.

Scrape weathered copper with an axe to collect Verdigris. A successful scrape yields 3–6 pieces; opening a copper door or canceling the scrape produces none.

Verdigris and Nether Quartz make Cyan Quartz. Polish it and combine it with the other recipe components to produce Quartz Semiconductors for signal components.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.signal_g:
Obtain a Conjunctor, Disjunctor, Inverter or Crossroad. Any one completes this entry.

Conjunctors require both side inputs; Disjunctors accept either side. Inverters provide the complementary signal, while Crossroads carry two crossing signal axes.

Use Ponder to inspect each component and a Create wrench to rotate or recover it. Crossroad strong output through solid blocks loses one signal level, so check analog signal strength when combining gates.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.magnetic:
Obtain 2 magnetic ports at once.

Opposite-facing magnetic ports couple Create rotation across a short, unobstructed gap. Put a real rotation source behind one port and the load behind the other.

The link transfers the source network's speed and stress capacity; it supplies no free power. Ship motion can break alignment or range, so keep the gap aligned throughout the mechanism's travel.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.spring_l:
Obtain 2 torsional anchors and 2 springs at once.

A torsional anchor behind each head of a paired Simulated spring transfers Create rotation between the endpoints. The springs used to craft the anchors are separate from this linking pair.

Provide an external drive and an appropriate load. The spring link shares that drive's stress budget rather than generating power; assembled and stationary endpoints can be connected.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.engines.gyro_sen:
Obtain 1 gyroscopic gearbox and 1 redstone converter at once.

A gyroscopic gearbox on a Sable body reports angular rate about its shaft axis. Connect a redstone converter to turn the signal into redstone strength.

This is a sensor with zero stress capacity, not a generator or an automatic stabilizer. The journal checks the equipment; it does not detect a working control circuit or a stable airship.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.flight.assembler:
Have at least 1 Physics assembler in your inventory at once.

The Physics Assembler turns a selected group of glued blocks into a Simulated Contraption. The assembled blocks can move together while remaining interactable.

Assembly does not supply lift or thrust. Include the propulsion, support and controls the structure needs before separating it from its fixed surroundings.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.flight.glue.desc:
Obtain Honey Glue.

Honey Glue connects blocks for Simulated Contraptions. Include the platform, supports, envelope and attached machinery in the intended assembly.

A visible contact between blocks is not enough to assume that every part belongs to the craft. Inspect the connections before assembly; an unattached part can fall away.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.flight.envelopes:
Have at least 4 envelopes of the same color in your inventory at once. Any color qualifies; mixed colors do not combine toward the count.

Envelope blocks form the roof and sides of an Aeronautics balloon. Lift depends on the volume filled with hot air; blocks inside the enclosure reduce the available space.

Provide a hot-air source and connect the envelope to the platform with supports and glue. An enclosure that is not part of the assembled craft can separate from it instead of lifting its cargo.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.flight.burner.de:
Have at least 1 Adjustable burner in your inventory at once.

An Adjustable Burner supplies hot air for a balloon. Its setting limits the volume of hot air supplied, in cubic metres; raising the setting beyond the envelope’s available volume adds no more lift.

The roof and sides must contain the hot air, while the bottom can remain open above the burner. Connect and glue the envelope, supports and platform into the same craft before assembly. Propellers or thrusters provide horizontal movement.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.flight.hot_air.d:
Receive Aeronautics' hot-air advancement near an envelope containing more than one cubic metre of hot air.

Build a connected envelope with enclosed sides and a roof, leaving the intended burner opening below. An Adjustable Burner supplies hot air to that volume.

The advancement confirms filled volume, not enough lift for the loaded craft. Compare lift and mass with the Contraption Diagram before leaving the ground.

Aeronautics can award nearby players within 10 blocks. This does not establish that you built the craft or completed a flight. An already completed advancement counts.
create_skyweave.journal.flight.diagram.d:
Have at least 1 Contraption diagram in your inventory at once.

The Contraption Diagram displays information about an assembled Simulated Contraption. Right-clicking the contraption with it lets you inspect the forces acting on the structure.

This helps investigate a craft that tilts, fails to lift or moves differently than expected. Use the diagram to inform adjustments to the build rather than adding propulsion without checking the cause.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.flight.propeller:
Have at least 1 Andesite Propeller or 1 Wooden Propeller in your inventory. Either item completes this condition.

Wooden and Andesite Propellers produce thrust when spun. They offer a propulsion option driven by Create rotation instead of a thruster's fuel or electrical input.

Thrust direction and placement matter to the craft as a whole. A propulsion layout needs to account for turning and balance as well as forward movement.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.flight.spin_prop:
Receive Aeronautics' advancement for powering a small propeller.

Connect a Wooden or Andesite Propeller to rotation. Nonzero rotational speed triggers the advancement for nearby players.

A spinning propeller is not proof of controlled flight. Test thrust direction, turning, lift and stopping near a safe landing area before loading cargo.

Aeronautics can award nearby players within 10 blocks. This does not establish that you built the craft or completed a flight. An already completed advancement counts.
create_skyweave.journal.flight.bearing.d:
Have at least 1 Propeller bearing in your inventory at once.

A Propeller Bearing spins an attached structure to produce thrust. Its propeller needs at least two valid sail-like blocks, and reversing rotation reverses the thrust direction.

Propeller thrust weakens at higher altitude in Aeronautics. A design tested close to a low island may need more thrust to operate around higher islands.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.main.food.title: Travel food
create_skyweave.journal.main.food.descri:
Obtain 8 bread or 8 baked potatoes at once. Mixed foods do not combine toward this condition.

Bread and baked potatoes are two renewable travel foods. Grow a crop near home and keep enough food for the outward and return journey.

These are examples rather than a required diet. Other foods remain useful, and preparing this batch does not prove that a farm is running.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.main.breeding.de:
Complete the Minecraft advancement for breeding an animal.

Breeding renews a local supply of animals instead of relying on repeated expeditions. Wheat breeds cows and sheep; other animals require their own food.

Keep the adults and their young contained before expanding the pen. Wool supports balloon envelopes, while leather is useful for gliders.

An already completed advancement counts. Completion records that advancement, not sustained production or a complete installation.
create_skyweave.journal.main.water.title: Water bucket
create_skyweave.journal.main.water.descr:
Have at least 1 Water bucket in your inventory at once.

A Water Bucket lets you establish water where you need it for building and processing. Water supports flowing-water power, fan washing and recipes that consume it as a fluid.

A bucket is a portable starting supply, while repeated fluid processing needs a replenishable source and a way to move it. Place that source where spills will not interfere with machinery or crossings.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.main.anvil.title: Equipment repair
create_skyweave.journal.main.anvil.descr:
Obtain an anvil.

An anvil repairs compatible equipment and combines enchantments at an experience cost. Check the result and level cost before committing an expensive tool.

Easy Anvils lets the workstation retain its inputs. Keep spare repair materials near frequently used equipment rather than waiting for it to break.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
Enchant an item at an enchanting table and complete its Minecraft advancement.

Enchanting improves equipment using experience and lapis lazuli. Bookshelves influence the offers, and Easy Magic keeps the table usable as a persistent workstation.

Review an offer before paying for it. Anvils provide a separate way to apply compatible enchanted books; this condition specifically records the table advancement.

An already completed advancement counts. Completion records that advancement, not sustained production or a complete installation.
create_skyweave.journal.main.travel_pack:
Obtain a standard or custom Traveler's Backpack and complete its inventory advancement.

A Traveler's Backpack keeps expedition equipment in a separate inventory. Equip it in the Accessories back slot and use the backpack control to open it; its starting leather tier provides 27 storage slots.

Keep return supplies apart from collected materials. Upgrade slots add functions such as crafting or fluid storage, while tool slots provide a separate way to exchange carried equipment.

On death, YiGD keeps the equipped backpack and its contents with your other recoverable items. Recover them from your grave; the backpack does not place a separate recovery block.

An already completed advancement counts. Completion records that advancement, not sustained production or a complete installation.
create_skyweave.journal.main.pack_sleepi:
Use the backpack's sleeping-bag control to deploy the bag and attempt to sleep.

The backpack's sleeping bag provides a place to attempt rest without carrying a separate bed. Quick deployment is enabled, so the backpack can remain equipped; allow space for the bag on solid ground.

Sleeping bags do not set your respawn point in this pack. This advancement records deployment and a sleep attempt, not a completed night; ordinary sleep restrictions still apply. Successful sleep also interrupts the sleepless nights used to encounter phantoms.

An already completed advancement counts. Completion records that advancement, not sustained production or a complete installation.
Use Traveler's Backpack's tool-swap action with an equipped backpack.

Store compatible equipment in the backpack's dedicated tool slots, then use its tool-swap control to exchange a slot with the item in your hand. Check Minecraft's Controls menu for the assigned binding.

Tool slots keep frequently used equipment available without filling the main storage grid. A swap does not repair the tool or preserve its durability; keep a replacement or repair supplies for longer trips. Completion records the swap action; it does not inspect the exchanged tool.

An already completed advancement counts. Completion records that advancement, not sustained production or a complete installation.
create_skyweave.journal.main.pack_fluids:
Use a hose to draw fluid into an equipped backpack's tank and complete its hose advancement.

The Tanks Upgrade provides two fluid tanks. Install one if the backpack does not already have tanks, select a tank and set the hose to draw mode before using it on a fluid source.

The configured leather-tier capacity is three buckets (3,000 mB) per tank. The hose can move fluids without supplying ship plumbing or fuel delivery automatically; tank contents and a usable source still matter.

An already completed advancement counts. Completion records that advancement, not sustained production or a complete installation.
create_skyweave.journal.manufacturing.qu:
Have at least 1 Quartz in your inventory at once.

Quartz is used with redstone to make rose quartz, which is polished for Electron Tubes. Those tubes are part of the Mechanical Crafter recipe, linking quartz access to Crushing Wheels and their processing routes.

Mining Nether quartz ore provides a route before Crushing Wheels are available. Later processing routes can supply more quartz, but do not assume they can supply the first tubes needed to build those wheels.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.manufacturing.cr:
Have at least 3 Mechanical crafters in your inventory at once.

Mechanical Crafters work together to craft recipes larger than a crafting table allows. Each crafter holds an ingredient, and the connected arrangement passes those ingredients toward its output.

The Crushing Wheels recipe needs 21 crafters arranged in a five-by-five square with the corners missing. Crafters are made three at a time, so seven batches supply that arrangement; the three required here are one batch.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.manufacturing.wh:
Have at least 2 Crushing wheels in your inventory at once.

Crushing Wheels process items between a pair of powered wheels. They handle recipes that a Millstone cannot, including the spruce-log route to pine resin.

The wheels must turn toward the gap where items enter. Supplying enough rotational power and collecting the outputs turns the pair into a reusable processing station.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.manufacturing.de:
Have at least 1 Deployer in your inventory at once.

A Deployer uses a held item on the block or item in front of it. It can automate actions such as placing blocks and applying ingredients during sequenced assembly.

Precision mechanisms use deployers to apply small cogwheels, large cogwheels and iron nuggets to a gold sheet. Keep the ingredients available and return the unfinished mechanism through the sequence until the recipe finishes.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.manufacturing.pr:
Have at least 1 Precision mechanism in your inventory at once.

Precision Mechanisms are components used in more advanced machines, including the Ion Thruster. They are made by repeatedly applying ingredients to a gold sheet with deployers.

The assembly recipe can produce byproducts instead of a finished mechanism. A production line therefore needs enough ingredients for repeated attempts and a way to separate completed items from unfinished ones.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.projects.photogr:
Expose a frame with an Exposure camera and receive its advancement.

A camera records a view onto loaded film. Use it to document a route, build or landmark that you want to recognize later.

An exposed frame is not yet a printed photograph. Development and printing turn the film into images that can be kept and displayed.

An already completed advancement counts. Completion records that advancement, not sustained production or a complete installation.
create_skyweave.journal.projects.print.d:
Print a photograph and receive Exposure's printing advancement.

Develop the exposed film and use the matching printing recipe to produce a photograph. Check the recipe viewer for the supplies required by the film and print.

Keep a record of a landing site or machinery layout alongside the finished build. The journal records the print event, not the subject or quality of the image.

An already completed advancement counts. Completion records that advancement, not sustained production or a complete installation.
create_skyweave.journal.projects.rail.de:
Obtain a Train Station and 16 Railway Tracks. The conditions are recorded independently.

Tracks provide a fixed route for trains once the supporting terrain or bridge exists. A station assembles and manages a train; the track items alone do not establish a working railway.

Begin with a short route on solid ground before building a long bridge. Stations, bogeys, controls and a complete connected route remain part of the project.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.projects.crossbo:
Obtain a crossbow.

A crossbow provides a ranged option for encounters around exposed terrain. Keep ammunition and a safe footing available rather than relying on melee reach over a drop.

This equipment entry does not start a raid. Automatic Hostile Skies raids remain disabled; any deliberate encounter needs its own preparation.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.travel.membranes:
Have at least 2 Phantom membranes in your inventory at once.

Phantom Membranes are ingredients in the Glider recipe. Phantoms provide a source after spending nights without sleeping, so the material does not require a Nether expedition.

This route involves fighting flying enemies rather than finding a rare machine component. Gather the membranes before making a crossing plan that depends on a glider.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.travel.glider.de:
Have at least 1 Glider in your inventory at once.

A Glider lets you turn height into travel across a gap. Its usefulness depends on the relative height of the departure point and the intended landing area.

A downhill crossing does not establish an easy route back to a higher island. Choose a landing area and a return method before committing to the flight.

Updrafts from supported heat sources can restore some height. Treat nearby crossings and landings as a separate problem from long-distance flight between island clusters.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
Have at least 1 Rope coupling in your inventory at once.

A Rope Coupling connects compatible rope endpoints, including a Rope Winch and a Rope Connector. Two Rope Connectors can also be linked, but two winches cannot connect directly.

This is the connection tool for the rope system rather than a powered winch itself. The installed rope system also allows sliding along a rope by right-clicking it while holding a wrench.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.travel.connector:
Have at least 1 Throwable rope connector in your inventory at once.

A Throwable Rope Connector places a rope connector at a distance. It extends the rope system to locations that are awkward to reach directly.

Its recipe combines a Rope Coupling with a Rope Connector. Plan the attachment points and the return route before treating a rope crossing as access to another island.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.travel.winch.des:
Have at least 1 Rope winch in your inventory at once.

A Rope Winch reels an attached rope in or out when supplied with rotational power. A Rope Coupling links it to a compatible Rope Connector.

The winch adds adjustable rope length to a tether or moving structure. It needs both an anchor arrangement and a power source; two winches cannot be linked directly to each other.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.alloy.d:
Have at least 2 Andesite alloy in your inventory at once.

Andesite Alloy is a construction material for Create's basic mechanical components. Shafts, casings and processing equipment make it a recurring requirement as machinery expands.

The basic crafting route combines andesite with iron or zinc nuggets. Either metal can support the early mechanical route, depending on the resources you have found.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.wheel.d:
Have at least 1 Water Wheel, 1 Large Water Wheel, or 1 Windmill Bearing in your inventory. Any one item completes this condition; it does not need to be placed or powered.

Water Wheels and Windmill Bearings provide rotational power for Create machinery. Water wheels use flowing water, while a windmill needs an assembled sail-bearing structure.

Use shafts and gearing to deliver the speed and direction each machine needs. A source can continue powering a dedicated workshop while other sources supply separate machinery or transport equipment.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.press.d:
Have at least 1 Mechanical press in your inventory at once.

A Mechanical Press turns suitable ingots into sheets using rotational power. Sheets supply recipes for components such as Electron Tubes and rope equipment.

A Depot or belt beneath the press supports individual-item processing. A Basin is used for its compacting recipes, so the arrangement depends on the recipe being performed.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.press_s:
Complete Create's sheet-pressing advancement.

Supply rotation to a Mechanical Press and place a suitable ingot on a Depot or belt beneath it. The processing advancement records a completed pressing operation.

Sheets support rope equipment, tubes and machine components. Keep the press available for repeat batches rather than dismantling it after the first sheet.

The machine credits its recorded player. An already completed advancement counts; the journal does not measure throughput or a complete production line.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.millsto:
Have at least 1 Millstone in your inventory at once.

A Millstone uses rotational power to grind items through its supported recipes. Its compact layout remains useful for a dedicated processing line even after Crushing Wheels are available.

Milling and crushing recipes can have different inputs and outputs. Check the recipe for the material you need; pine resin from spruce logs specifically requires Crushing Wheels.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.fan.des:
Have at least 1 Encased fan in your inventory at once.

An Encased Fan moves air when supplied with rotation. Passing that airflow through suitable blocks or fluids turns it into processing such as washing, smoking or blasting.

Washing is relevant to ore processing, including the chance to recover platinum from crushed raw gold. Keep the items in the affected airflow long enough for their recipe to finish.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.fan_pro:
Complete Create's fan-processing advancement.

Power an Encased Fan and pass its airflow through a processing medium. Water supports washing; other media support different recipes.

Keep an item with a matching recipe in the affected airflow until processing finishes. Recipe inputs and outputs matter more than the presence of a fan alone.

The machine credits its recorded player. An already completed advancement counts; the journal does not measure throughput or a complete production line.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.mixer.d:
Have at least 1 Mechanical mixer in your inventory at once.

A Mechanical Mixer processes ingredients in a Basin beneath it when supplied with sufficient rotational speed. Recipes can combine items and fluids, and some also require heat below the Basin.

Brass requires heated mixing; turpentine does not. For brass, the installed Propulsion Solid Burner can supply the heated state when fueled and placed below the Basin.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.mix.des:
Complete Create's Mechanical Mixer advancement.

Place a Basin beneath a powered Mechanical Mixer and supply a complete supported recipe. Some recipes need heat or fluids, while others only need items and rotation.

Andesite alloy is a useful early mixing recipe. Brass adds a heat requirement, and turpentine later connects the same machine to renewable fuel processing.

The machine credits its recorded player. An already completed advancement counts; the journal does not measure throughput or a complete production line.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.heat.de:
Obtain a Propulsion Solid Burner.

A fueled Solid Burner can heat a Basin for Create recipes. It provides an Overworld route to heated brass mixing without first capturing a blaze.

Leave room for fuel access and the Basin above it. This condition checks the burner item; producing a heated recipe still requires the mixer, ingredients and sufficient heat.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.brass.d:
Have at least 2 Brass ingots in your inventory at once.

Brass is used for components such as Brass Casings and Propeller Bearings. Producing it connects copper and zinc supplies to heated mixing in a Basin.

A fueled Propulsion Solid Burner can provide the heated state beneath the Basin. This gives the normal brass recipe a route that does not depend on capturing a blaze.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.linear_:
Obtain 1 linear bearing and 4 linear casings at once.

A linear bearing assembles a moving carriage above its face. Matching casings form a passive guide; use a real mechanical arrangement or gravity to move the payload.

Power on the moving carriage engages its brake. With the brake engaged and the payload aligned, use the casing with an empty hand to recover the bearing; its destination must be clear. These supplies do not prove that a working guide was built.

Ponder demonstrates assembly, braking and recovery. The tutorial illustrates the arrangement; the guide itself still needs an external force to move.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.hinged_:
Obtain 1 Hinge.

A Hinge joins a simulated payload to a base and rotates it through a limited arc. Its side shaft drives the joint through 90 degrees in either direction; the through shaft carries rotation into the attached mechanism.

Use glue to keep the intended payload connected and leave clearance for its full swing. Redstone unlocks the hinge by default, allowing it to move freely; the value panel changes this behavior. Holding the equipment does not demonstrate a working joint.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.ball_jo:
Obtain 1 Ball Joint.

A Ball Joint lets an attached simulated payload rotate about several axes. It permits 180 degrees of movement on the X and Z axes, while its shaft can pass rotation through to machinery on the payload.

The joint has no direct rotational drive. Gravity or another force moves the payload; redstone locks the joint by default, and the value panel changes the locking behavior. Use Ponder to review assembly, locking and shaft connections.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.flexibl:
Obtain 2 brass universal joint heads and 1 andesite universal joint rod at once.

Universal joint heads connect Create shafts across separate assembled physics structures. Both rod variants attach to brass heads; the rod you use determines the connection.

An andesite rod reaches farther and holds close to the length at which it was connected. A brass rod permits a shorter elastic connection. Both can strain and break when extended or compressed too far; leave room for the machinery to move within those limits.

Connect a shaft source and a load to use the link. This is an alternative to aligned magnetic ports or paired spring transmission, not an extra power source. These supplies do not demonstrate a working connection.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.pneumat:
Obtain 2 pneumatic connection heads and 1 pneumatic rod at once.

A pneumatic rod connects heads on separate assembled physics structures. Aim at the rod body and right-click to set target length, return force and stretch resistance. The normal rod operates from those settings without an external fuel, fluid or shaft supply.

Free mode allows the link to slide without actively returning to its target. A powered pneumatic regulator can select target length with redstone; shaft speed controls how quickly the target changes. This is distinct from a passive Linear Bearing guide.

Sneak-use a Create wrench on the rod body to disconnect it. Giant hydraulic rods offer pressure and flow controls, while hinge heads allow an end to swing about a pin axis. Keep the connection within its supported travel and leave clearance for the attached structure.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
create_skyweave.journal.workshop.rotatio:
Obtain 1 kinetic conversion bearing.

A kinetic conversion bearing turns the physical rotation of its attached structure into Create shaft output at the rear. Assemble the payload with the bearing, then provide a physical source of motion; crafting the bearing does not make it rotate.

Resistance opposes that motion, and the resulting output depends on measured rotation and the configured limits. Sneak-right-click the bearing to adjust its resistance. Use Ponder to review assembly and the output connection.

This provides a different role from the Linear Bearing gyroscopic gearbox, which reports angular rate with no stress capacity. The journal checks the equipment, not a working generator or sustained power production.

Placed blocks and items in containers do not count.
